action.F01.001: Adam Hruška? Your name is falling apart on my visitor list as we speak.
action.F01.002: So far I’m still here in one piece. What’s going on?
action.F01.003: Atlas has an exhibition in the hotel and a pavilion on Chopok. The cable cars are running normally, but our device is rewriting people’s records retrospectively.
action.F01.004: Who set it up like that?
action.F01.005: Viktor Korman, our founder. He didn’t switch it off even after my warning. Tamara will give you a reader, Boris the collection card, and Sára a pass and a ticket.
action.F01.x01: Falling apart? How can a name fall apart?
action.F01.x02: Letter by letter. A minute ago you were all there; now you’re just ‘Adam Hru’.
action.F01.x03: Retrospectively? So it even corrects things that happened long ago?
action.F01.x04: At the exhibition they call it normalisation. Whatever contradicts itself in the records, the device evens out. Names included.
action.F01.x05: Three people. Where do I find them?
action.F01.x06: Tamara has a desk in the lobby, Boris sits in the exhibition room, and Sára is at the customer centre.
action.F01.x07: A reader, a card, a pass and a ticket. And this morning I only set out to change a fuse.
action.F01.x08: I could do with a fuse myself. The kind that blows when someone ignores warnings.
action.F01.x09: Nobody’s made one of those yet. But I’ll try.
action.F01.x10: The reader first. Up in the pavilion I’ll contact you over the service channel.
action.F01.objective: At Hotel Grand Jasná, get the reader and the catalogue card, then the pass and ticket at the Biela Púť customer centre.
action.F01.journal: At Hotel Grand Jasná, get the reader and the catalogue card, then the pass and ticket at the Biela Púť customer centre.
action.F02.label: Borrow a reader for the original cassette
action.F02.001: Nina sent me. I need to read this old school cassette.
action.F02.002: Take this reader – it reads cassettes and service memory. You’ll get a coffee once the names stop vanishing from my orders.
action.F02.004: Only read the cassette – don’t fix anything on it. It’s an original.
action.F02.x01: Hi. You’re a repairer, aren’t you? Only repairers and small children look at my desk like that.
action.F02.x02: A repairer. Mostly tape recorders and anything that plays.
action.F02.x03: Let’s see. A school cassette with a handwritten label. I haven’t held one of those in years.
action.F02.x04: You’re telling me not to fix something?
action.F02.x05: I know it hurts. It hurts me too. But an original gets read, not repaired.
action.F02.x06: Fine. I’ll just look at it and suffer.
action.F02.x07: Welcome to the club. I sit on my hands with every original.
action.F02.journal: Tamara lent me a reader for the original cassette.
action.F03.label: Find collection Z-17 using the record
action.F03.001: The record checks out. Here is the collection’s catalogue card. Private recordings can only be opened by the curator, in service mode.
action.F03.002: What did Atlas discard from the collection first?
action.F03.003: Names that contradicted each other, pauses in speech, laughter. And one message from Mrs Kormanová. Apparently it was too ambiguous.
action.F03.005: Yes. And that’s exactly why her message should have stayed whole.
action.F03.x01: Good afternoon. I’m looking for collection Z-17. I have a confirmed handover for it from 2020.
action.F03.x02: Let me see. Two signatures, a date and the owner’s consent. An archivist couldn’t wish for a nicer piece of paper.
action.F03.x03: Laughter too? But laughter doesn’t bother anyone.
action.F03.x04: It bothers the normaliser. Laughter has no column, and anything without a column is noise to it.
action.F03.x06: He knows what’s in the catalogue. What’s missing from it, nobody can read in a catalogue.
action.F03.x07: Thank you. I’ll show the card to Sára.
action.F03.x08: Hold it by the edges and keep it away from coffee. Footnote: coffee is the archive’s worst enemy.
action.F03.objective: Show the catalogue card to Sára at the Biela Púť customer centre.
action.F03.journal: Show the catalogue card to Sára at the Biela Púť customer centre.
action.F04.label: Get the service pass and the ticket
action.F04.001: Nina has confirmed your service access to the pavilion. Here’s the pass and a return ticket for both sections of the cable car.
action.F04.003: Gondola to Priehyba, where you change for the Funitel to Chopok. The pavilion is by the Rotunda. Everything’s running today.
action.F04.004: An ordinary change, no leap across decades? I’ve been waiting all day for one of those.
action.F04.005: Keep the ticket – it’s valid for the way back too.
action.F04.x01: Good afternoon. Boris sent me with this card.
action.F04.x02: Good afternoon. I know the card. First I’ll write you into the visitors’ book in pen. Nobody vanishes from that.
action.F04.x04: You won’t. Tickets are like gloves – they always turn up in the other pocket.
action.F04.x06: Then you’ve got five extra chances. Have a good trip.
action.F04.objective: Hold the ticket to the reader at the Biela Púť bottom station.
action.F04.journal: Hold the ticket to the reader at the Biela Púť bottom station.
action.J02.label: Show the ticket and take the gondola to Priehyba
action.J02.002: First section: Biela Púť – Priehyba. An ordinary gondola, no node clock.
action.J02.objective: At Priehyba, change to the Funitel towards Chopok.
action.J02.journal: At Priehyba, change to the Funitel towards Chopok.
action.J03.label: Board the Funitel towards Chopok
action.J03.001: Your ticket is valid here too, go ahead. The doors only open once the cabin reaches the top.
action.J03.002: Only at the destination? Excellent. I’ve been through enough doors today with a different year behind them.
action.J03.x01: Good afternoon. Ticket, please. No skis?
action.J03.x03: That’s equipment too. It’s just harder to ski down on.
action.J03.objective: During the ride you can look out or chat to your fellow passenger; then finish the ride.
action.J03.journal: During the ride you can look out or chat to your fellow passenger; then finish the ride.
action.J04.label: Finish the ride and get off at Chopok
action.J04.001: Up there it’s always a slightly different world.
action.J04.003: Arriving at the station. Please exit once the doors open.
action.J04.x01: Colder and quieter. And phones get a worse signal up there – that’s the best thing about it.
action.J04.x02: I’ve got out of the habit of signals today.
action.J04.objective: By the Rotunda, photograph the normalisation panel with your phone, then go to the Atlas service pavilion.
action.J04.journal: By the Rotunda, photograph the normalisation panel with your phone, then go to the Atlas service pavilion.
action.F05.label: Photograph the normalisation panel
action.F05.001: The panel is public, so I’ll take a photo. It says: DIFFERENCE = DISCARD.
action.F05.002: The exact opposite of Gran’s sentence. The fault isn’t in the memories. It’s in the rule.
action.F05.journal: The normalisation panel is photographed: DIFFERENCE = DISCARD, the exact opposite of Mira’s rule.
action.F06.label: Compare the original cassette with the buffer
action.F06.001: I’m granting you access to the return buffer. The private record we’ll play only for Viktor.
action.F06.002: Connecting the reader. The cassette, Gran’s rule and the photo of the faulty panel.
action.F06.003: Withheld data can be restored. Switch the output to MONITOR.
action.F06.004: The diagnostics and the original message from Viktor’s mother are on your reader. You still need the trace from the stand by Vrbické pleso.
action.F06.005: I hope that isn’t another device that rewrites things.
action.F06.006: It isn’t. That stand only measures.
action.F06.x01: Nina here. Can you hear me? I can see you at the terminal.
action.F06.x02: I can. I can also hear my teeth chattering. It’s properly cold up here.
action.F06.x03: Withheld data? So it isn’t lost, it’s just waiting?
action.F06.x04: In the buffer, until someone confirms the write. So far nobody has confirmed it, not even Viktor.
action.F06.x05: How do I get to the lake?
action.F06.x06: Down by cable car, then on foot from the hotel. You’ll see the stand right by the path.
action.F06.objective: By Vrbické pleso, hold the chronometer to the passive stand and capture the reference trace.
action.F06.journal: By Vrbické pleso, hold the chronometer to the passive stand and capture the reference trace.
action.F07.label: Capture the local reference trace
action.F07.001: The exhibition’s stand on the path by the lake. The chronometer will read this place’s trace from it.
action.F07.003: The lake and the ice have stayed exactly as they were.
action.F07.objective: Go back up by cable car to the service pavilion and load the reference trace into the terminal.
action.F07.journal: Go back up by cable car to the service pavilion and load the reference trace into the terminal.
action.F08.label: Load the reference trace into the terminal
action.F08.001: The rule from 1962 and the local trace both match. I’ve signed the restore procedure.
action.F08.002: So: keep the exceptions, return the withheld records and switch off the write-back.
action.F08.003: There’s a switch on the terrace – set it to MONITOR. It’s a separate output; it won’t shut down the servers or the cable cars.
action.F08.004: Understood. No pulling out cables blindly.
action.F08.x01: Nina, the trace from the lake is in the terminal.
action.F08.x02: I can see it. It’s clean; nothing on it needs adjusting.
action.F08.x03: Exactly. That’s why my note hangs by the cables.
action.F08.x04: I saw it. Viktor probably didn’t read it.
action.F08.x05: He read it. He just thought it was meant for everyone else.
action.F08.objective: On the terrace by the Rotunda, switch the Atlas output to MONITOR.
action.F08.journal: On the terrace by the Rotunda, switch the Atlas output to MONITOR.
action.J05.label: Connect Tóno’s preserved return bridge
action.J05.001: Atlas’s separate connector. Oto’s bridge with Tóno’s swallow, thirty-eight years in the dry.
action.J05.002: The contact is holding. Now MONITOR will bypass the faulty write command.
action.J05.003: All the way here, led by a map a twelve-year-old Tóno drew.
action.J05.x01: That bridge is older than I am.
action.J05.x02: By quite a bit. I sealed it in a jar in December 1982.
action.J05.x03: Then give it my regards. And now the switch.
action.J05.objective: Now set the Atlas switch to MONITOR.
action.J05.journal: Now set the Atlas switch to MONITOR.
action.F09.label: Switch the output to MONITOR mode
action.F09.003: Nothing is vanishing any more. We have time for the repair.
action.F09.004: This is a very pleasant kind of silence.
action.F09.x01: The visitor list has stopped falling apart. You’re all there again.
action.F09.x02: Including the little hook on the š?
action.F09.x03: Hook and all. Now confirm entry to the chamber at the terminal.
action.F09.objective: In the pavilion, confirm entry to the chronochamber at the service terminal.
action.F09.journal: In the pavilion, confirm entry to the chronochamber at the service terminal.
action.F10.label: Verify MONITOR mode and open the chamber
action.F10.001: MONITOR mode confirmed. Chamber entry permitted.
action.F10.002: Viktor is inside. First he has to hear what the system threw away. Then we put in the four pieces of evidence.
action.F10.003: I’ll play him the whole recording. Pauses between the sentences and all.
action.F10.x02: Sitting at the table, staring into a glass of water. He poured it before the test started.
action.F10.x03: All right. I’ll stay on the channel, but I won’t interrupt.
action.F10.objective: In the chronochamber, play Viktor his mother’s unaltered message.
action.F10.journal: In the chronochamber, play Viktor his mother’s unaltered message.
action.F11.label: Play Viktor Lea’s original message
action.F11.001: You’ve switched off the write. Do you know how much could be lost now?
action.F11.002: I know what has already been lost. Listen to the original.
action.F11.004: In the edited version, all that was left was ‘call me’.
action.F11.005: Those pauses weren’t a fault. Nor was the fact that she didn’t want anything from you.
action.F11.006: Nina warned me. I let the test run because I wanted to believe the result.
action.F11.007: What’s left in the buffer can still be brought back.
action.F11.008: I agree. We’ll switch off the write for good and return the originals. And I’ll make public what I did.
action.F11.x01: Mr Korman, I’ve brought you a recording.
action.F11.x02: That’s how she always rang. When she had nothing to say.
action.F11.x03: The normaliser flagged them as noise. I approved it.
action.F11.objective: Put the evidence that belongs to each of the Origin, Voice, Consent and Return ports into it.
action.F11.journal: Put the evidence that belongs to each of the Origin, Voice, Consent and Return ports into it.
action.F12.label: Insert the verified imprint from 1962
action.F12.002: Gran’s rule. It was here long before the normaliser.
action.F12.x01: ‘Different data are not invalid data.’ My normaliser would have thrown that sentence out first.
action.F12.journal: The verified imprint from 1962 is in the Origin port.
action.F13.label: Insert the original school cassette from 1995
action.F13.002: And can I say something normal too?
action.F13.003: Today you can. And it’ll stay whole.
action.F13.x01: My mother recorded this cassette. I know that hiss in the background.
action.F13.x02: Her voice is on it too. All of it.
action.F13.journal: The original school cassette from 1995 is in the Voice port.
action.F14.label: Insert the confirmed handover from 2020
action.F14.002: Preserve, not erase. Signed by people who were really there.
action.F14.x01: Consent. I never asked anyone for that.
action.F14.journal: The confirmed handover from 2020 is in the Consent port.
action.F15.label: Insert the restore procedure from 2035
action.F15.002: The procedure is signed and the write is stopped at the switch.
action.F15.x01: Nina’s signature. I should have listened to her back then.
action.F15.journal: The signed restore procedure from 2035 is in the Return port.
action.F16.label: Verify the four testimonies
action.F16.001: I thought order meant one correct version.
action.F16.002: People have their own versions. Let’s leave them those.
action.F16.003: Restore ready. Confirm the final step.
action.F16.x01: Even the ones that contradict each other?
action.F16.x02: Those most of all. Gran would say: ‘What doesn’t match, we put side by side.’
action.F16.objective: Confirm the restore of the original records on the panel. You can finish side quests after the end of the story too.
action.F16.journal: Confirm the restore of the original records on the panel. You can finish side quests after the end of the story too.
action.F17.label: Restore the records and go home
action.F17.001: My name is Adam Hruška. I was there. And I’m here too.
action.F17.002: I confirm my consent to the restore.
action.F17.003: Original records restored. Write-back switched off.
action.F17.x01: Viktor Korman. I started the test.
action.F17.objective: The story is over. The time windows stay open, so you can finish the side quests.
action.F17.journal: The story is over. The time windows stay open, so you can finish the side quests.
action.Q8A.001: Recipient: repair shop by the bench with the dog. There is no repair shop at these coordinates today.
action.Q8A.002: I’ll try to find out. Hang on to the parcel for now.
action.Q8A.x01: The bench with the dog? What dog?
action.Q8A.x02: Not specified. Dogs in the area: two alive and one on a poster. None is sitting on a bench.
action.Q8A.x04: This possibility was not in the brief. Probability of success increased to thirty per cent.
action.Q8A.x05: You walk, I wait. My driving success rate in snow is forty per cent.
action.Q8A.journal: Očko is looking for the recipient: a repair shop by the bench with the dog. I’ll find out where it is today.
action.Q8B.label: Compare the old address with the bench
action.Q8B.001: A ceramic dog and the sign DRUHÝ ŽIVOT – ‘second life’. On a note underneath: ‘Tamara, during the exhibition, in the lobby of Hotel Grand Jasná.’
action.Q8B.002: So the repair shop has just moved. I’ll ask Tamara whether the parcel is really hers.
action.Q8B.journal: The bench with the dog belonged to Tamara’s workshop. Tamara is now in the lobby of Hotel Grand Jasná.
action.Q8C.label: Show Tamara Očko’s request
action.Q8C.001: Yes, that parcel is mine. Last year I had a stall by the lake; this year I’m at the Grand. Here’s a confirmation with the new address.
action.Q8C.002: I’ll take it to him. A new address and no bench with a dog – Očko can manage that.
action.Q8C.x01: Tamara, are you expecting a parcel? A delivery robot called Očko is looking for you.
action.Q8C.x02: Očko? He’s been looking for me since the autumn. Show me that request.
action.Q8C.x03: And tell him that when he comes, he’ll get a coffee. Even though he claims he doesn’t drink it.
action.Q8C.x05: For anyone who brings me parts. Rules are rules.
action.Q8C.objective: Take the confirmation to Očko at Biela Púť.
action.Q8C.journal: Take the confirmation to Očko at Biela Púť.
action.Q8D.label: Give Očko the repair shop’s confirmation
action.Q8D.001: Recipient confirmed. New point: repairer’s desk in the lobby of Hotel Grand Jasná.
action.Q8D.002: The last hundred metres sometimes take a person.
action.Q8D.003: Thanks have no navigational value. I will keep them anyway.
action.Q8D.x01: Here’s the confirmation from Tamara. She’s not by the lake any more; she’s in the hotel lobby.
action.Q8D.x03: And Tamara sends her thanks. With a coffee.
action.Q8D.x04: Coffee: incompatible. Saving the offer in the folder Unnecessary But Kind.
action.Q8D.journal: Očko has a new address: Tamara’s repairer’s desk in the lobby of Hotel Grand Jasná.
action.Q9F.001: Here’s my first drawing from 1982. Next to it is a photo of the laptops from 2020 and the names of the people who helped.
action.Q9F.002: So no changing the world overnight.
action.Q9F.003: No. Just a lot of small things that might never have happened otherwise.
action.Q9F.x01: By the way, I have the notebook in my bag. Someone once told me they’d like to see it.
action.Q9F.x02: And will you show it to me?
action.Q9F.x03: Only the first page. I’m still drawing the rest.
action.Q9F.x04: Is that the notebook from the exhibition?
action.Q9F.x05: Not that one. The fourth. The first three are full.
action.Q9F.journal: Jana is exhibiting her first drawing next to the laptops from 2020 and the names of the people who helped.
entry.S41.001: Jasná, fifteen years later, in the depths of winter. Good thing I’ve still got my coat from December 1982.
look.S41.ROBOT: Očko the delivery robot, its wheels stuck in the snow. It has a parcel; it just doesn’t know who it belongs to.
look.S41.ambient 1: Two benches under the snow. Only someone in waterproof trousers can sit on them.
look.S41.ambient 2: Wooden signposts: Priehyba, Chopok, Biela Púť. The one for Biela Púť points at where I’m standing.
look.S41.gate: The turnstile for the gondola to Priehyba. It won’t let me through without a valid ticket.
exit.S41.to_S67.locked: I need a valid ticket for the cable car. Without one, the turnstile won’t even talk to me.
conn.S41.S67.label: Cable car Biela Púť – Priehyba
conn.S41.S67.locked: I need a valid ticket for the cable car. Without one, the turnstile won’t even talk to me.
entry.S42.001: Hotel Grand Jasná, with half a metre of snow on the roof. By the exhibition stand someone is waiting, as if for me.
look.S42.NINA: Nina looks as if she’s spent three hours explaining something obvious to someone with a bigger budget.
look.S42.ambient 1: A spruce outside the hotel, more snow than needles. One prod and the snow would bury the reception desk too.
look.S42.ambient 2: A brass luggage trolley. Two suitcases and not a single pair of skis – these people came for the exhibition.
entry.S43.001: A repairer’s desk in a hotel lobby. Next holiday, I’m packing a broken tape recorder too.
look.S43.TAMARA: Tamara takes things apart so that they can be put back together.
look.S43.ambient 1: A coffee machine with a display. Before it makes the coffee, it tells me how it’s feeling.
look.S43.ambient 2: Tamara’s system has two shelves: ‘might come in handy’ and ‘was looking for that yesterday’.
entry.S44.001: A hotel function room full of archive boxes. Outside the window people ski; in here people quietly turn pages.
look.S44.BORIS: Boris looks at a missing record the way you look at someone who wasn’t sent an invitation.
look.S44.JANA35: Jana. She once stood with her schematic at a school exhibition; today she’s come to an exhibition of her own free will.
look.S44.ambient 1: Paper books. Not one of them has ever rewritten a single line by itself.
look.S44.ambient 2: A red bookmark in an open book on the counter. Someone stopped reading here, and the book will wait for them.
entry.S46.001: The information centre. A good place to start for someone who already has trouble with today’s date.
